items.title: Locomotion and comfort source gate
steps: Write docs/standards/locomotion/source-manifest.json naming only admitted positive public sources (engine locomotion documentation, platform comfort guidelines, maintained open-source locomotion implementations) with role, admitted claims, limits, and license boundary per source; mark every URL as not fetched unless a person confirmed it.

Write docs/standards/locomotion/verification-contract.md with a Core gate (teleport, snap turn, smooth turn, continuous move, and comfort policy as engine-light intents and immutable state with stable failure codes) and a Unity adapter gate (thin binding to the XR Interaction Toolkit locomotion providers with explicit diagnostics for every by-name resolution), plus a claim ceiling that names motion-sickness, comfort, and device behaviour as device-evidence only.
Write docs/standards/locomotion/README.md with a disposition row for every lesson in the lessons register, and docs/standards/locomotion/admission.draft.json in the shape of the audio draft.
Add a NEXT-LOCOMOTION-COMFORT candidate to docs/foundry/queue/next-batch.json with state proposal, no package_ids, and no placeholder text.
items.evidence: The four artifacts in the tree and a merge-readiness verdict with repository_contract pass on the pull request.

items.title: Locomotion and comfort staged Core and Unity adapter
steps: Read docs/standards/locomotion/verification-contract.md, which WI-001 produced, then author staging/locomotion/com.lingkyn.locomotion.core and com.lingkyn.locomotion.unity with package.staging.json, asmdefs, Runtime sources, NUnit EditMode tests, and a domain-only sample, modelled on staging/audio.
Write docs/standards/locomotion/coverage-map.json mapping every contract clause to named tests; every listed test must exist and every test must be listed.
Write staging/locomotion/README.md with the status line, the what-is-here table, the promotion steps, and the statement that the code is authored and unexecuted.
items.evidence: validate_coverage_map_claims passes on the new map with no allowlist entry.

items.title: Scene flow source gate
steps: Write the source manifest, verification contract (Core gate: scene set identity, load and unload intents, transition state machine with fade and hold, error recovery with stable codes; Unity adapter gate: thin binding over additive scene loading with explicit diagnostics), README with lesson dispositions, and admission draft for the Scene flow family.
Add a NEXT-SCENE-FLOW candidate to the queue with state proposal and no package_ids.
items.evidence: The four artifacts in the tree and a passing repository contract.

items.title: Scene flow staged Core and Unity adapter
steps: Read docs/standards/scene-flow/verification-contract.md, which WI-003 produced, then author the staged Core and Unity adapter packages with tests and a sample, modelled on staging/audio.
Write the coverage map and the staging README.
items.evidence: validate_coverage_map_claims passes on the new map with no allowlist entry.

items.title: XR UI shell source gate
steps: Write the source manifest, verification contract (Core gate: panel, wrist and hand menu, pointer and gaze routing as renderer-neutral intents and state; adapter gates for UGUI and UI Toolkit as siblings with one injectable skin seam mapping the shared design-language tokens), README with lesson dispositions, and admission draft for the XR UI shell family.
State how the Inventory presentation adapters become one client of the shell without transferring any Inventory evidence.
Add a NEXT-XR-UI-SHELL candidate to the queue with state proposal and no package_ids.
items.evidence: The four artifacts in the tree and a passing repository contract.

items.title: Source manifests of every family are machine-checked
steps: Generalise validate_inventory_source_manifest into a rule that validates docs/standards/*/source-manifest.json for every family with the same admission, HTTPS, role, evidence, and license-boundary requirements, keeping the Inventory rule's behaviour unchanged.
Add fix hints, a test module, and move the register row from self-declared to machine-checked.
items.evidence: The register row names the new function and the tests; the repository contract passes on every existing manifest or the exact findings are allowlisted with the removal comment.

items.title: API surface inventories are derived, not typed
steps: Add a rule that compares each docs/standards/<family>/api-surface.md type list with the public type declarations found in that family's Runtime sources, reporting every missing or extra type.
Correct the three inventories where the rule finds drift, add fix hints and tests, and update the register row.
items.evidence: The register row names the new function and the tests.

items.title: CI binds a governance change to its deliberation record
steps: Make merge_readiness.py discover the deliberation record for a governance change from the changed files (a record added or modified under docs/governance/deliberations/ in the candidate) when --deliberation-record is not passed, and make the CI job rely on that discovery.
Add a test where a governance change without any record is blocked and one with an open record inside its window is blocked, and update the register's first known gap.
items.evidence: validate_workflow_security still passes and the new tests are green.

items.title: Cold-start receipt template and schema
steps: Define a receipt an outside contributor or Agent fills after following start-here.md from a fork: tool used, commit started from, minutes per step, the pull request URL, the verdict, and what was confusing; the schema forbids not_tested and requires a public commit and pull request.
Validate committed receipts under docs/validation/cold-start/ with a validator rule and a test.
items.evidence: The template validates against the schema and the start-here page links both.

items.title: First cold-start receipt from outside the maintainer account
steps: From a fork, follow start-here.md with any tool (a person, or an Agent such as a coding assistant in an editor or a terminal), land one routine change, and commit the filled receipt.
items.evidence: A receipt naming a merged pull request from an account other than the maintainer.

items.title: Run the Unity gates and bind every profile to the current commit
steps: Run python scripts/run_unity_gates.py for every live package on the default-branch commit and commit the receipts, result XML, and locks under docs/validation/evidence/<profile>/.
Move every compatibility profile to that commit; fix any test the run turns red before rebinding.
items.evidence: unity_evidence reports pass in the merge-readiness verdict.

items.title: Promote Localization from staging
steps: Follow the five promotion steps in staging/localization/README.md; the admission signature is a maintainer decision.
Delete staging/localization once the packages are live.
items.evidence: A verified compatibility profile for each Localization package at the promotion commit.

items.title: Promote Audio events from staging
steps: Follow the promotion steps in staging/audio/README.md; the admission signature is a maintainer decision.
Delete staging/audio once the packages are live.
items.evidence: A verified compatibility profile for each Audio package at the promotion commit.

items.title: Inventory world-space UI device receipt
steps: Build the XR composition at a public commit, run the plan on one named headset, fill the receipt with every binding the schema requires, and validate it with --device-lab-receipt before committing.

items.title: Required checks, auto-merge, license secret, release tags
steps: In the repository settings: make repository-contract and merge-readiness required checks on the default branch and enable auto-merge; add the Unity license secret the unity-consumer-tests workflow names.
Create the Git tags named in the batch registry at the evidence commits.
Record the date each setting was made in docs/contributing/merge-readiness.md so the tree carries the claim.
items.evidence: A green merge-readiness check visible on a pull request and the tags resolvable from a fresh clone.

items.title: Five certified good-first-issue items
steps: Pick five routine items from python scripts/open_work.py --markdown that need nothing but a clone, and open one Issue each with setup context, exact change and test locations, bounded size, and a named shepherd, as CONTRIBUTING.md requires for the certified subset.
items.evidence: Five Issues carrying the good first issue label that each meet the certified subset.

items.title: Pair every standard with both a source manifest and a verification contract
steps: Write docs/standards/design-language/verification-contract.md with the clauses a token set can actually be checked against (every token named in the standard exists in the JSON, the reference hierarchy is explicit, and a claim ceiling routing legibility and contrast to a Device Lab receipt), modelled on docs/standards/locomotion/verification-contract.md.

Write docs/standards/foundations/source-manifest.json in the field set the other family manifests use, naming only admitted public sources for the project-initializer and xr-baseline capabilities, with a review_note stating the URLs were not fetched.
Empty FAMILY_SOURCE_MANIFEST_UNVERIFIED_CLAIMS in scripts/validate_repository.py and update the pinning test so the real repository produces no suppressed message.
items.evidence: validate_family_source_manifests passes with an empty allowlist.

items.title: Live tuning source gate
steps: Write the source manifest, verification contract (Core gate: a closed tunable kind set, an immutable registry by explicit registration, set, reset, snapshot, apply, and export intents on an immutable state with deterministic replay, and a bridge to and from the design-language token JSON; Unity gate: explicit bindings to skin assets, live apply through the existing skin seams with diagnostics, an injectable export sink so Play-mode changes survive, and a panel that is one client of the XR UI shell), README with lesson dispositions, and admission draft for the Live tuning family.

State the claim ceiling: the family proves plumbing (a change reaches the bound value and exports to the asset that owns it); whether a value looks right on a headset is a Device Lab receipt, never a package claim.
Add a NEXT-LIVE-TUNING candidate to the queue with state proposal and no package_ids, and a rank row in ROADMAP.md after the XR UI shell.
items.evidence: The four artifacts in the tree and a passing repository contract.

items.title: Live tuning staged Core and Unity adapter
steps: Author staging/live-tuning/com.lingkyn.live-tuning.core (TunableId, the closed TunableKind set, TunableRegistry, TuningState, the set, reset, reset-all, snapshot, apply, and export intents with the result codes the contract names, deterministic replay, and the design-language token bridge) and com.lingkyn.live-tuning.unity (binding records to skin assets, live apply through the existing skin seams, an injectable export sink with a device JSON writer and an Editor asset writer, and a tuning panel that is a client of the XR UI shell with a UGUI fallback), with package.staging.json, asmdefs, NUnit EditMode tests, and a domain-only sample, modelled on staging/scene-flow.
Write docs/standards/live-tuning/coverage-map.json mapping every contract clause to named tests; every listed test must exist and every test must be listed.
Write staging/live-tuning/README.md with the status line, the what-is-here table, the promotion steps, and the statement that the code is authored and unexecuted.
items.evidence: validate_coverage_map_claims passes on the new map with no allowlist entry.
